If the integrator instead treats a company role begun in the final doctoral year as a pre-degree job continued under rule 1, the first new job is Duke, July 2008, Assistant Professor at a business school (tenure-track by convention). He joined the NPS faculty in 1965, about a year before the 1966 degree, and served there as a naval officer; his title on joining is not documented. Judge (17 Oct 2026): placementYear corrected from 1965 to null. Each faculty section of the 1966-67 catalogue states that the year in parentheses is the year of joining the Postgraduate School faculty, so 1965 dates his arrival, not his assistant professorship; the 1965-66 catalogue (hdl.handle.net/10945/31695, read through the Calhoun API) does not list him, or the other 1965 arrivals Lindsay, McMasters and Schrady, so it predates his arrival; and in both catalogues the department's other junior naval officer without a doctorate, Lt(jg) Samuel H. Wagner says that after two years at MIT he 'accepted a position at Stanford prior to receiving a degree', earned the PhD in 1960, and in 1960 joined McKinsey & Company as an OR consultant to its San Francisco office, later leaving California for Yale's Department of Administrative Sciences; the INFORMS presidential-portrait page dates the Stanford Graduate School of Business post 1957-1967 and Yale 1967-1976, and the UNC Kenan-Flagler tribute calls McKinsey a career-long consulting relationship begun in 1960. The INFORMS education section and the Mathematics Genealogy Project (dissertation 'Statistical Management of Inventory Systems', advisor Robert Solow) give the doctorate as MIT 1960, not the imported Stanford. The Stanford post began about three years before the degree and continued to 1967; no opened source gives his Stanford title before or after 1960, so whether Stanford converted the post on completion is unknown, and the McKinsey consulting post began in 1960, after the degree and seven years before Yale. The Yale professorship of 1967 therefore cannot be shown to be the first new post-PhD job, and no other first job is established. Earlier review (2026-10-16): the same Stanford-before-degree and McKinsey-1960 conflict was found and the MIT doctorate was noted without a primary MIT record. Verifier: a consulting post (McKinsey, 1960) began between the degree and the Yale appointment, and the Stanford title history is undocumented, so Yale (1967) is not established as the first job.

Audit (2026-10-17): evidenceNote changed from no statement of a pre-degree Dalarna role to this statement, because the overlap must be recorded (R3: the earlier role is kept in the note). A South East European University news item of 26 April 2010 says that after his 2009 Dalarna master's (best master's thesis prize) he 'was admitted to the Swedish University as the only Albanian young assistant', and Libris shows the 2014 Örebro doctoral thesis also registered in Dalarna University's repository (urn:nbn:se:du-13797), so he held a junior post, apparently at Dalarna, and a Dalarna affiliation during the 2010-2014 doctorate. The title and terms of that post (doctoral studentship, assistant or adjunct) are not given. The bio presents the tenure-track Computer Engineering post as following the doctoral studies, so the row treats it as the post given on completion (R3), start year unknown. If the 2010 post was a regular job rather than a doctoral-stage role, R5 would apply instead, and the first new employer would be Örebro University (Senior Lecturer from 2016-04, ORCID). Consistency check (2026-10-17): placementYear changed from null to 2014, position from null to 'Assistant Professor (tenure track)' and evidenceUrl from https://fp.alfaisal.edu/profile/mmemedi to his Alfaisal CV, because the CV (March 2026 version; the February 2024 version has the same entries), read in its work-experience and education sections, dates the Dalarna posts: 'PhD student', Dalarna University, Borlänge, from 2010 (80% research for the doctoral education, 20% teaching), then 'Assistant Professor (tenure track)', Dalarna University, from 2014, then Örebro University Business School from 2016, with the Örebro PhD in Information Technology in 2014 (an IT consultancy at Nordforce Technology from 2008 precedes the doctoral post).
